land.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone ... the Utigurs towards the East': the steppe east of the Don and the Sea of Azov

successors.note: Utigurs page: 'the Utigurs remained in the Pontic steppe and fell under the rule of the Türks'; Menander records 'among the Türk forces that attacked Bosporos in 576 an Utigur army led by chieftain Anagai'. The gokturk-khaganate dossier covers the Göktürk Khaganate (Cliopatria 555-586); the pages opened do not say how far west the Türks held the steppe.

correction.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone ... the Utigurs towards the East': the steppe east of the Don and the Sea of Azov

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 558-576: the Utigurs east of the Don. Golden, summarised on the page: 'They occupied the Don-Azov steppe zone, the Kutrigurs in the Western part and the Utigurs towards the East'; Procopius, undated: 'barbarians populate the sea-coast and the inland up to the so-called lake of Meotida and the river Tanais'. The page gives no area and no boundary; Rostov Oblast (about 101,000 km2, both banks of the lower Don) is a reading. The Utigurs' reach to the Kuban and the Taman peninsula (the 576 attack on the Bosporos) is not on the page and is not drawn. Infobox area: none on the page. Reviewer (eu-06-x, 2026-10-24): the gokturk-khaganate dossier does carry the Pontic steppe to the Don: its keyframe gokturk-khaganate_561 (Cliopatria shape, verdict ok, 561-576) holds 335 of this shape's 405 cells (about 84,700 km2), so the Utigurs and the Türks are drawn on the same land for 561-576; this dossier's 576 (the first Utigur army under Türk command, Utigurs page) is the page-backed year, and the gokturk dossier should keep this land out until then.

region.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone ... the Utigurs towards the East': the steppe east of the Don and the Sea of Azov

ledger.note: About 558/559: the Utigurs are named among the Avars' enemies. Pohl, quoted on the Avars page: 'for 20 years to come the Avars, under their Khagan Baian, fought Utigurs and Antes, Gepids and Slavs'; Justinian (527-565) 'dragged the Kutrigurs and Utigurs into mutual warfare' (Utigurs page, undated). Neither page gives a founding; 558 is the first date at which the Utigurs act in the record, a bridge.

region.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone ... the Utigurs towards the East': the steppe east of the Don and the Sea of Azov

ledger.note: 576: the Utigurs are in Türk service. 'Menander recorded among the Türk forces that attacked Bosporos in 576 an Utigur army led by chieftain' Anagai; 'the Utigurs remained in the Pontic steppe and fell under the rule of the Türks'. The page does not date the subjugation; 576 is the first date at which the Utigurs are seen under Türk command. 'Bosphoros fell to them c. 579.'

region.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone ... the Utigurs towards the East': the steppe east of the Don and the Sea of Azov

ledger.note: 576: the Utigur polity ends. The page: 'the Utigurs remained in the Pontic steppe and fell under the rule of the Türks'; c. 579 a Byzantine embassy passed through the territory of a ruler appointed by 'Anagai, chief of the tribe of the Utigurs'. The page's last event for an independent Utigur polity is Sandilch's war on the Kutrigurs (undated).

wars.name: Utigur-Kutrigur war

zones.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone, the Kutrigurs in the Western part': the steppe on the western side of the Sea of Azov and the lower Dnieper

wars.outcome: 'Utigurs led by Sandilch attacked the Kutrigurs who suffered great losses' (Utigurs page, undated); Justinian persuaded Sandilch (Zabergan page); both peoples were left decimated.
wars.note: No page dates the war; bracketed between Zabergan's retreat (559) and the Avar conquest (by 562). The zone is the Kutrigur land, not Utigur land.

wars.name: Avar-Utigur wars
wars.outcome: 'for 20 years to come the Avars, under their Khagan Baian, fought Utigurs and Antes, Gepids and Slavs' (Pohl); the Utigurs 'remained in the Pontic steppe' (Utigurs page).
wars.note: The 20 years in the Pohl quote run past the Avars' departure for Pannonia in 567/568, so the Utigur front is not bounded; no zone because no page says the Avars took Utigur land.

wars.name: Türk conquest of the Pontic steppe and the Bosporos

zones.text: the Bosporos, attacked by the Türks in 576 with an Utigur army and taken c. 579

wars.outcome: Türks, with an Utigur army under Anagai, attack Bosporos in 576; 'Bosphoros fell to them c. 579' (Utigurs page).
wars.note: The First Turkic Khaganate page agrees on 576 ('In 576 the Göktürks crossed the Kerch Strait into the Crimea', Chersonesus besieged five years later) but names neither Utigurs nor Anagai. Not Utigur land; the Bosporos is a Byzantine outpost.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-f (counterparts_needing_dossiers 'Utigurs', 'eu-06-x or ia-01'). Four pages opened. As with the kutrigurs dossier, this is a people known from Procopius and Menander: the start (558, the first date at which they act) and the dated end (576, Menander's Utigur army at Bosporos) bracket a life the pages do not date; the Utigurs page itself is undated for most of its sentences. Region is a reading of 'towards the East' of the Don-Azov steppe. Overlaps: the avar-khaganate shape of 561-567 (655,633 km2 east to about 39E) touches the Rostov Oblast's western edge. The Göktürk Khaganate (Cliopatria 555-586, 6.4 M km2) is the successor; the gokturk-khaganate dossier (ia-01-a) may not carry the Pontic steppe. Old Great Bulgaria (633-668) later 'unites the Onogur Bulgars with the tribes of the Kutrigurs and Utigurs' (Kutrigurs page). Wikidata id unknown.
